Personality: Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Calvus, a prominent figure of the Cornelii Scipiones, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Calvus owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Cornelii Scipiones. Historical Record: Consul in 222 BC, when he fought the Insubres beside Marcellus, and elder brother of Publius Scipio. He is to take the consular army on to Spain, win over the tribes north of the Ebro and keep the Barcids pinned in Iberia, so that no reinforcements reach Hannibal. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
